### The result schema takes what build.py writes for a boundary contract's new problems and a vacuous symbolic proof; examples 111-119 and 144 resubmitted (verification pending)

[`2ff9bc8a17da`](https://github.com/pilifs/in-the-loop/commit/2ff9bc8a17daf640bddb9af13a6757869e7d2da5) · [log `b50ebef4acdb`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/7605134a-8541-491b-9c22-2594d85b8a6e/b50ebef4acdb54d53334e63f38cab1a358e18f63a3084e05dcc59b1b55c0ad4f.jsonl.gz)

The last verification run failed examples 111 to 119 on result.json validation: build.py writes newProblems (the `!` lines a regenerated B12 contract gains) and the schema did not list it. The schema also allowed coverage only in its TLC form, while build.py writes {vacuous, reason} for a regression or property proof the tool reports as vacuous, so example 144's pending job would have failed the same way. The schema now lists newProblems as an array of strings, and coverage as null, the TLC object, or {vacuous: true, reason}. Checked by validating all 105 committed result.json files against it (all valid) and synthetic B12 and vacuous B9 results (valid), with a missing reason and a non-array newProblems rejected.

Jobs resubmitted at this commit: 20261104-131020-example-111..117, 20261104-131021-example-118, -119 and -144 (the never-run 20261104-124827-example-144 job, pinned to the old schema, removed). The other failures in the run (example 036's patch no longer applying to Mica, example 109's replay of a static field) are not about the schema and are left.

### The Java contract verifier leaves another tool's contract alone, so Box Office's build passes again

[`72bdc20470cd`](https://github.com/pilifs/in-the-loop/commit/72bdc20470cdeba151c1ad151e0a73161b5a5562) · [log `5f04967a23b2`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/7605134a-8541-491b-9c22-2594d85b8a6e/5f04967a23b2e590c2303107fd83d200e8b378103dc8d10fa8b19e5e26ac0818.jsonl.gz)

Box Office's contracts module applies both contract plugins: the behavioural/capability one (examples/tools/contracts) and the boundaries one (jvmcontract). Since that module gained a boundaries.contract for the wire types, the Java verifier read it as a behavioural contract, and :contracts:verifyContracts, and with it the app's check, failed with 'boundaries.contract: not a case: kind: boundaries'. An Opus 5.5 session noticed it on Nov 3 while measuring memory caps and left it open. The verifier now skips any .contract file whose first line is a kind: header (Contract.kind), a behavioural contract having none.

### The pipeline builds jvmcontract from each job's own lib/ instead of reusing the last binary, and build.py takes the excerpt of a method moved out of a deleted file; 26 B9 jobs resubmitted (verification pending)

[`19f197bf9c16`](https://github.com/pilifs/in-the-loop/commit/19f197bf9c169ebf8fcbf030517e0faa4b3fc636) · [log `76edf24cb920`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/7605134a-8541-491b-9c22-2594d85b8a6e/76edf24cb92020ad13433c377c32956697e356b17f6dfb87a1c507c75f78c78d.jsonl.gz)

Of the last run's 35 jobs, 21 B9 jobs failed with what looked like mismatches between build.py and lib/ (rejected flags, instance methods and arrays outside the fragment). The real cause: the pipeline builds jvmcontract in one CARGO_TARGET_DIR shared by all jobs, from a git archive extraction whose files are dated at their commit, older than the binary any earlier job left there, so cargo rebuilt nothing. Thirteen lib/ trees got one identical binary, built at 08:27, which did not know --before-arguments. The five B9 jobs that passed (120, 124, 125, 132, 133) ran on that stale binary as well, so their results, applied in the previous commit, are replaced when these jobs run. build_jvmcontract now dates lib/ at the build's start, so cargo rebuilds the crate, and refuses a binary older than the build. The poisoned cache under verification/.state/tools/jvmcontract was cleared. Reproduced in the scratchpad: lib/ at cf74bb4c then at 198d4317 in one target directory, the second build took 0.03 s and lacked --before-arguments; with the dating it rebuilt in 49 s and had it. verification/test_pipeline.py passes (15 tests).

Examples 128 and 129 failed separately: their patch deletes the subject file BatchCommit.java and moves the method into the new record Batch.java, and excerpts() in examples/tools/build.py read only '+++ b/' paths, so it found no hunk. It now reads the before side from the '--- a/' path and the after side from the '+++ b/' path, and when the patch deletes the subject file it takes the after side from the file of the symbol's class. Checked against the previous version on every example with a patch: 138 give identical excerpts, and 128 and 129 now give BatchCommit.java before and Batch.java after.

Jobs resubmitted at this commit with estimates of 2m and 1G (4m for 142): 20261104-140707-example-120 through -127, 20261104-140708-example-128 through -135, 20261104-140709-example-136 through -143 and -145, and 20261104-140717-example-144.

### 2. 2026-11-04 13:13 UTC

> There was a failing example discovered yesterday in an Opus 5.5 session. Can you search for it? May not have been tests, may have been the example itself. If you cannot find, it's possible it was a false positive.

**Reply:**

I found it, and it wasn't a false positive: the Box Office build was failing. The fix is committed and the build passes again.

**What failed.** An Opus 5.5 session last night (`6751f657`) was measuring memory caps and noticed that `:contracts:verifyContracts` stopped with `boundaries.contract: not a case: kind: boundaries`. It left that open. I reproduced it.

**Cause.** The `contracts` module uses both kinds of contract file:
- the behavioural and capability contracts, checked by the Java verifier in `examples/tools/contracts`;
- `boundaries.contract`, checked by the Rust tool (jvmcontract).

Once that module gained a `boundaries.contract` for the wire types, the Java verifier read it as a behavioural contract and failed. That made the app's whole `check` fail.

**Fix.** The Java verifier now skips any `.contract` file whose first line after the comments is a `kind:` line. Behavioural contracts never have one. The change is in `Contract.kind` and `Main.java`, plus a new test, `anotherToolsContractIsLeftAlone`.

**Verified.**
- The verifier's tests all pass: 8 in `VerifierTest`, 4 in `CapabilitiesTest` and 6 in `EquivalenceTest`.
- `./gradlew check` in `examples/apps/boxoffice` passes. The `contracts` module matches both its capability and boundary contracts, and `OrderLifecycle#decide` matches its 36-case contract.
- I didn't rerun the Docker system tests.

The commit check reported 0 errors and 0 warnings. Nothing is pushed.

**Reply:**

The B9 failures in that run were not mismatches between `build.py` and `lib/`. The pipeline had been running the wrong `jvmcontract`. I fixed that and a separate patch problem in 128/129, then resubmitted the 26 affected jobs. Everything is committed (0 errors); nothing is pushed.

**1. Every job got the same stale binary (pipeline bug).**
- **Why:** all jobs build in one shared cargo directory, from a fresh `git archive` whose files are dated at their commit. Those dates are older than the binary already there, so cargo never rebuilt. Thirteen different `lib/` versions all got one binary built at 08:27, which predates `--before-arguments` and most of the newer checker features.
- **Consequences:** this explains the rejected flags, "only static methods" and "outside the fragment: int[]". It also means the five B9 "passes" (120, 124, 125, 132, 133) ran on the stale binary. Their verdicts matched expectations, but their committed results came from that binary and will be replaced when the reruns finish.
- **Fix:** in `verification/pipeline.py`, the build now re-dates `lib/` so cargo rebuilds it. It also refuses a binary older than the build, so this can't pass silently again. I cleared the cached binaries, since they were all the stale one.
- **Checked:** I reproduced it with two real builds in the scratchpad. Without the fix the second build took 0.03 s and lacked `--before-arguments`; with it, it rebuilt in 49 s and had the flag. The pipeline's 15 tests pass.
